question: Can finite quantum theory be reconstructed as a representation of ordinary, generally non-Markovian stochastic dynamics over definite configurations, with wave functions and Hilbert-space objects demoted from ontology to mathematical tools?

key_findings.claim: The basic dictionary represents any finite stochastic transition matrix by modulus-squared complex amplitudes and packages its one-time probabilities into density-matrix notation.
key_findings.evidence: For each conditional probability Gamma-ij(t<-0), choose Theta-ij with modulus square Gamma-ij. Then rho(t) = Theta(t) diag(p(0)) Theta-dagger(t) has diagonal entries p-i(t), so p-i(t) = tr(P-i rho(t)); for a definite initial configuration the corresponding column of Theta plays the role of a state vector and gives the Born-form identity.

key_findings.claim: A Kraus construction and Stinespring dilation embed the stochastic map in a larger unitary model, but this is a nonunique dilation rather than proof that the original transition matrix is itself unistochastic.
key_findings.evidence: Column-isolating operators K-beta satisfy the Kraus identity, after which the configuration space is enlarged from N to at most N-cubed elements so a unitary can reproduce the original transition probabilities after marginalizing a formal ancilla. The paper then focuses 'without any real loss of generality' on this dilated unistochastic process, although ordinary stochastic matrices need not be doubly stochastic or unistochastic on the original space.

key_findings.claim: For a differentiable unitary lift, the von Neumann, Schrödinger, and Ehrenfest equations follow exactly after defining the Hamiltonian from that unitary.
key_findings.evidence: The paper sets H(t) = i hbar (partial-t U) U-dagger and differentiates the lifted density matrix, state vector, and expectation formula. This is mathematically correct, but the unitary and its phases have already been selected by the dilation/lift, so the calculation recovers standard unitary identities rather than deriving a unique Hamiltonian from transition probabilities alone.

key_findings.claim: The manuscript identifies quantum interference with cross terms measuring failure of a chosen unistochastic transition family to compose through an intermediate time.
key_findings.evidence: Although relative unitaries obey U(t<-0)=U(t<-t')U(t'<-0), their entrywise modulus squares do not generally obey the Chapman-Kolmogorov composition. Equation 43 expresses the discrepancy as the usual amplitude cross terms and applies the interpretation to double-slit trajectories.

key_findings.claim: Nondivisibility alone is not an intrinsic characterization of quantum interference because the intermediate map is obtained from a nonunique phase lift rather than from the specified stochastic process.
key_findings.evidence: At a non-conditioning time t', the underlying model does not supply p(i,t|k,t'). The paper instead defines Gamma(t<-t') as the modulus square of a relative unitary; different admissible phases can leave Gamma(t<-0) unchanged while altering the relative unitary and pseudotransition comparison. Generic classical memory also violates Chapman-Kolmogorov without exhibiting operational quantum interference.

key_findings.claim: Ideal system-environment record formation produces a division event, a diagonal reduced density matrix, and under additional repetition assumptions a discrete Markov chain.
key_findings.evidence: The derivation assumes perfect configuration-environment correlation at t', unitary subject/environment factorization afterward, and marginalizes the environment to obtain a composable subject kernel. Regular events plus time-homogeneous relative dynamics yield powers of one stochastic matrix; the same algebra removes off-diagonal density-matrix elements.

key_findings.claim: The discussion's transition-matrix criterion for entanglement captures correlation after interaction but is not sufficient to distinguish quantum entanglement from classical correlation.
key_findings.evidence: Entanglement is identified with failure of the composite cumulative stochastic kernel to tensor-factorize. Classical interacting or common-cause stochastic systems can also have nonfactorizing kernels; no Bell/CHSH model, separability criterion, no-signalling proof, or account of measurement-setting independence is provided, and locality and causation are explicitly deferred.

key_findings.claim: The measurement construction reproduces ideal projective Born probabilities and collapse-as-conditioning, conditional on assuming a tailored quantum-style interaction.
key_findings.evidence: For a self-adjoint matrix A-tilde, the paper assumes a composite SDE unitary that maps its eigenbasis into perfectly correlated subject, pointer, and environment records. Born probabilities, a post-measurement eigenprojector, and the uncertainty relation then follow. Existence of precisely this coupling is the criterion making the matrix an 'emergeable,' so the operational content is assumed in the measurement dynamics rather than forced by the original stochastic kernel.

key_findings.claim: The specified first-order kernels do not constitute a complete stochastic process for multi-time experiments or a unique trajectory ontology.
key_findings.evidence: The author explicitly groups together processes that share p(i,t|j,t0) while leaving all higher-order conditionals and whole-trajectory probabilities unspecified and possibly varying between runs. Quantum experiments include sequences of interventions whose probabilities depend on multi-time correlations; reproducing each as one larger initial-to-final composite experiment does not supply a single consistent intervention-sensitive law.

key_findings.claim: The strongest ontological and application claims remain untested in the reviewed paper.
key_findings.evidence: There is no worked Bell experiment, sequential-control example, continuous configuration-space construction, relativistic field theory, numerical simulation, empirical fit, finance/turbulence application, or prediction differing from textbook quantum theory. Locality, causation, quantum gravity, and nonphysics applications are future work.

method.core_idea: Lift finite transition probabilities to complex amplitudes, express one-time probability propagation in Hilbert-space notation, and use unitary dilation plus idealized composite interactions to reinterpret standard quantum phenomena as features of indivisible stochastic dynamics.
method.mechanism: Entrywise square roots yield an amplitude matrix; column Kraus operators yield a quantum channel; Stinespring enlarges the configuration space to a unitary process; relative unitaries generate cross terms, while environment records create division events and measurement pointers implement spectral projectors.
assumptions: Finite discrete configuration spaces are adequate, possibly after unquantified coarse-graining.
First-order conditional probabilities from selected conditioning times suffice for all empirical quantum predictions despite unspecified higher-order laws.
A nonunique Kraus/Stinespring dilation can be treated as a physically meaningful correspondence rather than only an embedding.
Phase choices and ancillary degrees of freedom do not introduce operational ambiguity beyond a legitimate gauge freedom.
Composite measurement interactions of the exact eigenstate-pointer-environment correlating form exist for candidate emergeables.
Contextual and apparently nonlocal stochastic laws can reproduce Bell-compatible quantum statistics while retaining the desired explanatory advantages.
Ideal record orthogonality, post-interaction factorization, and repeated division events adequately approximate realistic environments.

techniques.role: Factors nonnegative stochastic entries as modulus-squared complex amplitudes.
Rewrites one-time marginalization and expectations as trace formulas.
Constructs a CPTP representation from normalized amplitude columns.
Embeds a general finite stochastic map into a larger unitary process with a formal ancilla.
Identifies failed stochastic composition with amplitude interference terms.
Uses orthogonal environmental records to recover effective composable stochastic dynamics and decoherence.
Represents non-diagonal observables through ideal spectral correlations with a device and environment.
Updates future subject probabilities by conditioning on a definite pointer configuration.

evaluations.result: An entrywise complex lift and density matrix reproduce the original one-time transition probabilities exactly.

evaluations.metric: existence and dimension of unitary dilation
evaluations.result: A Kraus/Stinespring construction embeds the process into a unitary model on at most N-cubed configurations.
evaluations.baseline: Possibly nonunitary amplitude matrix on the original N configurations.

evaluations.result: Defining H from U yields the Schrödinger, von Neumann, and Ehrenfest equations identically.

evaluations.setting: Chosen intermediate time in a unistochastic lift
evaluations.result: The discrepancy equals amplitude cross terms of the standard interference form.

evaluations.metric: factorization of subject probabilities after t'
evaluations.result: The interaction creates a division event and diagonal reduced density matrix; regular homogeneous events give a discrete Markov chain.

evaluations.metric: pointer outcome probabilities and conditional post-measurement state
evaluations.result: The assumed spectral-correlating unitary reproduces Born probabilities and Lüders-like collapse as conditioning.

evaluations.setting: Empirical quantum, Bell, sequential-control, continuous-space, or applied stochastic benchmark

limitations: The core stochastic object contains only selected two-time kernels; higher-order conditional and trajectory probabilities are deliberately unspecified.
Pointwise modulus-square data do not uniquely determine complex phases, a Hamiltonian, relative unitaries, or responses to arbitrary interventions.
Stinespring dilation enlarges the configuration space with a formal ancilla and is many-to-one; this supports representability but not automatically an ontological equivalence.
The finite discrete treatment only asserts that continuous spaces can be handled and supplies no measure-theoretic construction in this paper.
Calling generic nondivisibility interference does not distinguish classical memory from operational quantum interference.
Failure of tensor factorization is not sufficient for quantum entanglement and does not address Bell inequalities or relativistic local causality.
The measurement derivation assumes the tailored unitary, orthogonal pointer records, environment correlation, and effectively rank-one projective structure needed to obtain the result.
General POVMs, instruments, degeneracy, weak/continuous measurements, adaptive interventions, and incompatible sequential measurements are not developed.
Exact division events require ideal correlations; approximation errors and observable bounds are not quantified.
No empirical, numerical, predictive, or domain-application evidence tests the proposed advantages over standard quantum formalisms or process tensors.
Locality and causation—the central constraints on any definite-configuration hidden-variable account—are left to future work.
The arbitrary entrywise phase freedom is called gauge, but invariance of all emergeable measurement statistics under that full freedom is not established in this version.
failure_modes: Two stochastic models share every specified first-order kernel but disagree on a sequential intervention, so the correspondence cannot choose the quantum prediction.
Different phase lifts of the same transition probabilities yield different relative maps, Hamiltonians, or measurement couplings.
A classical non-Markovian process is labeled as showing quantum interference solely because Chapman-Kolmogorov composition fails.
A classically correlated composite kernel is labeled entangled despite admitting a separable common-cause explanation.
Bell correlations are reproduced only by silently introducing nonlocal, measurement-dependent, or contextual transition laws.
An intended observable lacks the tailored physical interaction required to correlate its eigenbasis with a pointer, so it is not actually measurable.
Imperfect environmental records leave residual coherences and prevent an exact division event or collapse update.
A continuous or relativistic system requires infinite-dimensional dilation, domains, or locality conditions not covered by the finite proof.
The enlarged ancilla carries the missing information needed for unitarity, undercutting the claim that it need not be physically meaningful.
A bespoke composite kernel reproduces one complete experiment but fails composition-consistency when experiments are recombined or controls are changed.
reusable_insights: Separate representation theorems from ontological equivalence: track which extra phases, ancillas, and intervention rules the representation introduces.
For non-Markovian theories, validate complete multi-time controlled statistics rather than only state propagation from one initial time.
Treat phase nonuniqueness as gauge only after proving invariance of every operationally allowed preparation, transformation, and measurement.
Distinguish classical correlation, kernel nonfactorization, quantum entanglement, and Bell nonlocality with explicit operational tests.
A measurement reconstruction should derive or constrain the coupling, not assume exactly the spectral correlation that yields the Born rule.
Environment-induced divisibility is a useful bridge between non-Markovian and Markov models, but approximation quality should be bounded.
Encoding a stochastic model in Hilbert space may be computationally useful even when it supplies no new physical prediction.
Negative and deformed-probability representation theorems can often be evaded through contextuality; state explicitly where that contextuality enters.
open_questions: Can one specify a Kolmogorov-consistent hierarchy of multi-time probabilities that reproduces all adaptive quantum instruments without importing Hilbert-space phases as extra law?
Which phase and dilation choices are operational gauge-equivalent, and what minimal stochastic data select an equivalence class?
Can the framework construct and analyze an explicit CHSH experiment while identifying exactly which Bell assumption fails?
What necessary and sufficient stochastic criterion distinguishes entanglement from ordinary nonfactorizing classical correlations?
How does the correspondence extend rigorously to continuous spectra, unbounded operators, relativistic quantum fields, and changing particle number?
Can realistic approximate division events yield quantitative trace-distance or prediction-error bounds?
Does the Hilbert lift improve simulation or inference for a real non-Markovian process versus process-tensor, state-space, or tensor-network methods?
Can emergeable measurement interactions be derived from a restricted physical dynamics rather than postulated case by case?
Does the approach produce any falsifiable prediction or compression advantage beyond standard quantum theory?

competitive_landscape.title: The Stochastic-Quantum Theorem
competitive_landscape.difference: Barandes's later paper formalizes generalized stochastic systems and states a precise unitary-representation theorem. It strengthens the mathematical dilation claim, while the operational uniqueness, multi-time, and ontological questions audited here remain separate from representability.

competitive_landscape.title: Quantum Systems as Indivisible Stochastic Processes
competitive_landscape.difference: This sequel deepens the same author's treatment of gauge invariance, dynamical symmetries, and Hilbert-space dilations—precisely areas handled only briefly in the reviewed version. It is continuation rather than independent corroboration.

competitive_landscape.title: Quantum stochastic processes and quantum non-Markovian phenomena
competitive_landscape.difference: Milz and Modi formulate quantum stochastic processes as compatible process tensors that predict joint statistics for arbitrary instruments across times. Their hierarchy directly exposes the information missing when only first-order conditional probabilities are specified.

competitive_landscape.title: Non-Markovian quantum processes: Complete framework and efficient characterization
competitive_landscape.difference: The process-tensor framework maps sequences of experimentally implementable controls to output states, handles system-environment correlations, and is tomographically reconstructible. It offers completeness and intervention semantics absent from the reviewed two-time-kernel equivalence class.

competitive_landscape.title: Reconstruction of quantum theory on the basis of the formula of total probability
competitive_landscape.difference: Khrennikov already reconstructs interference amplitudes, Born form, Hilbert space, and operator observables from contextual Kolmogorov probabilities. The reviewed paper's distinctive ingredient is indivisible dynamics and dilation, but the broader ordinary-probability reconstruction claim has substantial prior art.

competitive_landscape.title: Informational derivation of Quantum Theory
competitive_landscape.difference: Chiribella, D'Ariano, and Perinotti reconstruct finite-dimensional quantum theory from operational composition and purification principles, including transformations and systems. Their axioms are less ontologically classical but constrain the entire operational theory rather than embedding isolated stochastic kernels.

competitive_landscape.title: Recovering the Quantum Formalism from Physically Realist Axioms
competitive_landscape.difference: Auffèves and Grangier pursue a physically realist reconstruction of Hilbert-space quantum formalism from contextual and extravalence principles. It is a direct competing route to realist axioms without identifying generic stochastic nondivisibility with quantumness.

competitive_landscape.title: Frame representations of quantum mechanics and the necessity of negativity in quasi-probability representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Ferrie and Emerson prove that broad frame representations of full quantum state/effect calculus require negativity or a deformed probability rule. The reviewed framework avoids this exact theorem through contextual, dynamics-dependent emergeables and a Hilbert lift, so that escape route should be made explicit rather than read as a noncontextual classical representation.

competitive_landscape.title: Bell on Bell's theorem: The changing face of nonlocality
competitive_landscape.difference: Brown and Timpson analyze Bell local causality for stochastic beable theories. This is a necessary constraint on any definite-configuration ordinary-probability account; describing entanglement as nonfactorization does not identify how Bell-local causality or another premise is relinquished.

competitive_landscape.title: Quantum-embeddable stochastic matrices
competitive_landscape.difference: Shahbeigi et al. characterize when stochastic matrices arise from memoryless continuous-time quantum evolution and find non-embeddable families. The reviewed construction is broader because it permits non-Markovian dynamics and dilation, but that breadth also makes its physical constraints and testability weaker.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Stochastic-Quantum Correspondence
competitive_landscape.difference: Calvo develops examples, fields, measurement, and a classical-limit account while noting a problem in extending the treatment to continuous bases. It confirms active follow-up but also underscores that the reviewed paper's finite-to-continuous step is nontrivial.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after all 38 pages and eleven primary-source comparisons: the entrywise-amplitude/Kraus/dilation dictionary is an elegant synthesis, and the manuscript gives a coherent definite-configuration interpretation of familiar unitary algebra. Its strongest theorem is representational. The claim of an exact physical correspondence is stronger than what the reviewed version establishes because phases and dilation are nonunique, higher-order intervention statistics are unspecified, ideal measurement dynamics are assumed, generic nonfactorization is not quantum entanglement, and Bell/locality analysis is postponed. The work is a serious foundations proposal, not yet a complete operational reconstruction or empirically validated stochastic alternative.
reviewer_notes: Reviewed all 38 pages of the 2025 accepted manuscript, including equations 1-95, dilation, interference, division/decoherence, entanglement, measurement, collapse, uncertainty, interpretation, and references. The source text contained embedded null bytes but had full 38-page coverage. Checked eleven primary arXiv sources through 2026-08-23, including the author's formal successors and independent multi-time/process-tensor, reconstruction, contextuality, and embedding work.
